title: Synthesio vs Talkwalker vs Meltwater: Enterprise-Grade Coverage Compared
summary: Synthesio, Talkwalker, and Meltwater all claim enterprise-grade coverage in 2026 — but only some of it is verifiable. Here's what's confirmed vs. claimed.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Synthesio, Talkwalker, and Meltwater all pitch themselves as "enterprise-grade" social intelligence platforms, and all three back that up with real scale — but the coverage each one claims isn't equally verifiable in 2026. Talkwalker's numbers are the most consistently confirmed: 150 million+ sources, 192 languages, and Blue Silk AI video/image recognition included at every tier, no partnership dependency. Meltwater backs its claims with the strongest named-customer proof of the three (Shiseido, Yves Rocher, Unilever) and genuine, already-shipped TikTok video transcription via its own Marketing Partners integration. Synthesio's raw numbers are the largest on paper — 80 billion signals a year, 2,000+ ecommerce sources — but its most newsworthy 2026 coverage claim, video intelligence, now has a real asterisk: the partner who built it was acquired by a direct Synthesio competitor four months later, and neither company has said what that means for Synthesio's customers. None of the three publishes real pricing; all three require a custom enterprise quote.


Every enterprise social-intelligence vendor says "comprehensive coverage" on its homepage. The word does no work — it's not falsifiable, and it doesn't tell you what's actually confirmed versus aspirational.


Synthesio, Talkwalker, and Meltwater are worth comparing specifically on this axis because they make some of the boldest scale claims in the category, and because one of them — Synthesio — is in the middle of a live, unresolved question about whether its own flagship 2026 coverage claim still holds up. That makes this trio a useful test case for a question every enterprise buyer should be asking in 2026: how much of "enterprise-grade coverage" can you actually verify before you sign?


This comparison breaks each platform's coverage claims into what's confirmed by primary sources, what's third-party estimated, and what's genuinely unresolved — then shows where a video-native layer changes the picture entirely.

## How Each Platform's Coverage Claims Hold Up


### Synthesio: The Biggest Numbers, and the Biggest Open Question


Synthesio has been an Ipsos company since Ipsos acquired it for $50 million in October 2018 (Source:[GlobeNewswire, 2018](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2018/10/30/1639419/0/en/Synthesio-Acquired-By-Ipsos-Reinforcing-Social-Media-Intelligence-Capabilities.html) ). It positions itself as "the shortest path to insight," claiming to process 80 billion social signals annually across 10+ search platforms and 2,000+ ecommerce sources, with a GenAI layer called "Signals" (Source:[Synthesio, 2026](https://www.synthesio.com/) ). It holds a solid 4.3/5 on G2 across 151 reviews, and reviewers consistently praise its customer support (Source:[Capterra, 2026](https://www.capterra.com/p/160240/Synthesio/) ).


The coverage claim that matters most in 2026, though, is video. On January 19, 2026, Synthesio announced an "official platform partnership" with ViralMoment, covering on-screen text, spoken audio, visuals, and actions across TikTok, Reels, YouTube, and YouTube Shorts in 76+ languages (Source:[Synthesio, 2026-01-19](https://www.synthesio.com/blog/ipsos-synthesio-viralmoment-partnership-brings-leading-video-intelligence-to-our-clients/) ). Four months later, on May 28, 2026, Sprinklr — a direct Synthesio competitor — acquired ViralMoment's assets outright (Source:[Sprinklr Newsroom, 2026-05-28](https://www.sprinklr.com/newsroom/sprinklr-acquires-viralmoment-to-define-the-next-era-of-multimodal-customer-intelligence/) ). No source — not Sprinklr's release, not Synthesio's own blog, not independent trade coverage — addresses what happens to the Synthesio partnership. A direct check of Synthesio's site in August 2026 found zero mention of video intelligence, ViralMoment, or Sprinklr, despite the site actively promoting other newer features.


**Where Synthesio's coverage is confirmed:** Broad social, search, and ecommerce data breadth, and Ipsos market-research credibility no pure-tech competitor can match.


**Where it's unconfirmed:** Its single most newsworthy 2026 capability — video coverage — now depends on a partner that's been absorbed into a competitor, with zero public clarity either way.


### Talkwalker: The Most Consistently Verifiable Numbers


Talkwalker's core claim is Blue Silk AI, a proprietary engine trained on 3 trillion data points handling sentiment and emotion analysis across 192 languages, with image recognition matching against 30,000+ predefined models for logos, scenes, and objects — and coverage spanning 150 million+ sources across social, news, and broadcast (Source:[Talkwalker, 2026](https://www.talkwalker.com/products/bluesilkai) ). Unlike Synthesio's video story, Talkwalker's video/audio AI is built in-house and included across every tier — not gated behind a partnership or premium add-on.


The Hootsuite acquisition (announced April 2024, closed Q2 2024) folded Talkwalker's technology into Hootsuite Listening while Talkwalker continues to sell standalone for enterprise buyers (Source:[Hootsuite, 2024](https://www.hootsuite.com/newsroom/press-releases/hootsuite-agrees-to-acquire-talkwalker) ). That's a stability signal most competitors in this trio can't claim right now — Talkwalker's coverage roadmap sits inside a company with its own independent survival already settled, rather than depending on an outside partner.


**Where Talkwalker's coverage is confirmed:** Video and image recognition shipped and non-gated, 192-language sentiment coverage, and no third-party dependency risk on its core AI stack.


**Where it's weaker:** Its video/audio AI is described generically as covering "audio and video social media posts," not confirmed as purpose-built specifically for short-form platforms like TikTok or Reels the way a video-native tool is.


### Meltwater: The Strongest Named-Customer Proof


Meltwater's differentiator has never been social listening in isolation — it's the combination of press monitoring, journalist databases, broadcast clippings, social listening, and influencer marketing (via Klear, now "Meltwater Influencer Marketing") in one platform (Source:[Meltwater, 2025](https://www.meltwater.com/en/blog/klear-is-officially-part-of-meltwater) ). Its video coverage claim is the one in this trio backed by a real, already-shipped feature: TikTok video transcription via its Marketing Partners integration, combining keyframe analysis with speech-to-text.


Where Meltwater separates itself from both Synthesio and Talkwalker is named-customer proof. It has real, checkable customers publicly attached to its case studies — Shiseido, Yves Rocher, and Unilever among them (Source:[Meltwater, 2026](https://www.meltwater.com/en/customer-stories/shiseido) ) — the strongest public proof of enterprise deployment in this comparison. Pricing is quote-based, with analyst estimates putting median spend around $25,000/year, ranging from roughly $6,000 (Starter) to $150,000+ (Enterprise) (Source:[Vendr, 2026](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/meltwater) ).


**Where Meltwater's coverage is confirmed:** Global news and broadcast breadth, genuine shipped TikTok video transcription, and the strongest publicly named enterprise customer roster of the three.


**Where it's weaker:** UX complexity is consistently flagged in reviews, and its video intelligence is narrower in scope (TikTok-specific) than Talkwalker's broader in-house video/image stack.


## The Real Lesson: Coverage Claims Need a Confirmation Status, Not Just a Number


Line up all three vendors' coverage claims and a pattern emerges that a simple feature grid hides: **raw scale and verified scale are not the same thing.** Synthesio's numbers are the biggest on paper, but its most important 2026 claim is currently unconfirmed at the source. Talkwalker and Meltwater both ship real, working video capability today — but neither is a video-content-first platform built around that capability from day one; it's an add-on layer (Talkwalker's generic "audio and video" claim) or a single-platform integration (Meltwater's TikTok-only transcription).


That distinction matters more as brand conversations keep moving into video where nothing is typed. ## How to Choose: Decision Framework


Skip the feature grids and the marketing copy — ask which of these describes your actual buying criteria.


-


**If you want Ipsos-grade market-research credibility and can tolerate an unresolved video-coverage question →** Synthesio, but confirm ViralMoment's current status directly before signing.


-


**If you want the most consistently verifiable enterprise coverage numbers, with video/image AI included at every tier →** Talkwalker.


-


**If PR and social listening sit on the same team and you want the strongest named-customer proof in this comparison →** Meltwater.


-

## Key Takeaways


-


Synthesio's coverage claims are the largest on paper (80B signals/yr, 2,000+ ecommerce sources) but its 2026 video-intelligence claim is unconfirmed after its partner, ViralMoment, was acquired by direct competitor Sprinklr in May 2026


-


Talkwalker's coverage is the most consistently verifiable of the three — 150M+ sources, 192 languages, video/image AI shipped in-house and included at every tier


-


Meltwater backs its coverage claims with the strongest named-customer proof (Shiseido, Yves Rocher, Unilever) and genuine, already-shipped TikTok video transcription


-


All three require custom enterprise quotes — none publish a public rate card


-


None of the three is a video-content-first platform; their video capability is a partnership (Synthesio, currently uncertain), a generic in-house layer (Talkwalker), or a single-platform integration (Meltwater)


## Conclusion


Synthesio, Talkwalker, and Meltwater all earn their place on an enterprise shortlist — but "enterprise-grade coverage" means something different, and something differently verifiable, for each. Synthesio trades on Ipsos credibility and raw data volume, with a real open question hanging over its newest capability. Talkwalker's numbers hold up best under scrutiny. Meltwater backs its claims with the clearest named-customer proof.


None of the three, though, was built around video as the primary signal — and that's where brand conversations in beauty, F&B, and fashion increasingly live.
